triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: All eight rules of the below-floor Switzerland heading 9903.02.83 started at 2026-02-15 rather than the 2025-11-14 date Annex II made the heading effective, so the 15 percent floor top-up was absent for the first three months of the heading's life.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 3 (li-87) and its below-floor sibling index 4; note its paired module ch-82 (index 8) had the mirror-image error (too early), so pre-fix the Switzerland floor pair was internally inconsistent — above-floor live from August, below-floor not until February. Source verified in the same Annex II text. Diff: 8 effective_from changes, two effective_period atoms per rule, summary and corpus_citation_paths; no formula change.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff changes `effective_from` from '2026-02-15' to '2025-11-14' on all eight rules of the Switzerland below-floor heading 9903.02.83 module, which is a version-window change, not provenance bookkeeping (the added proof atoms and the second corpus_citation_path are the supporting provenance for exactly that date change; no formula, parameter value, input, or output moved). Reading the cited provision through the pinned release (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, provision us/rulemaking/federal-register/2025-12-18/2025-23316) confirms Annex II states "Effective with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on November 14, 2025, subchapter III of chapter 99 ... is modified as follows:" and item 7 "New headings 9903.02.82-9903.02.91 shall be inserted in numerical sequence" — so the source fixes the heading's start at 2025-11-14 and the pre-fix 2026-02-15 disagreed with it (the string "February" does not occur anywhere in the notice). I tried the competing readings and none survive: it is not mechanical because effective dates are explicitly excluded from that class, and it is not untraceable_branch because the more specific effective-date kind governs a wrong effective_from; the encoded meaning genuinely differed for goods entered 2025-11-14 through 2026-02-14, where the 15 percent floor top-up would not have fired.

The same -2026-02-15/+2025-11-14 pair appears eight times, once per rule, so the whole module's window moves coherently; there is no partial/mixed-date state left behind and no effective_to is introduced. Both added proof-atom excerpts are verbatim in the pinned provision text (the "New headings" excerpt is source line-wrapped as "New headings 9903.02.82-9903.02.91 shall be inserted in \nnumerical sequence", consistent with the commit's note about FR hard-wrap normalization). Two caveats for the reviewer, neither of which changes the verdict but both of which affect how the case reads as a corpus exemplar: (1) the module was introduced earlier in the same PR #1197 (add 8fd1c00ed -> r1 fix 75a367787 -> this r2 fix 4d2856a95 -> r3 fix 0ae98bd52), so this defect was caught in pre-merge review rather than shipped to main — the corpus should be explicit about whether review-caught defects count; (2) roughly 140 of the 184 diff lines are added effective_period proof atoms and the corpus_citation_path -> corpus_citation_paths widening, which are provenance; only the eight one-line date changes carry meaning. A later commit (0ae98bd52, "exclusion judgments dated from EO 14257 effectiveness") re-dates some judgments again, so if the corpus also samples that commit, watch for double-counting the same effective-date family in this module.
